blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.
blocks.zh: 物理AI任务的模型,如机器人和自主驾驶,不需要仅仅用语言来说明理由. 它们可以使用视觉图点,边框,以及轨迹来表示空间目标并预测运动. 然而,自动递减的愿景语言模型一次生成一个协调符号,使更丰富的预测越来越昂贵。 我们引入了VFlash,一种通过Flash Primitive Decoding进行快速,准确的视觉规划的方法. VFlash利用已知的视觉原始体结构来共同预测它们的坐标,使用一个轻量级的起草器,在一个前传中生成一个完整的原始体. 该布局适应原始人的类型,维度,以及长度,支撑紧凑的盒子和长,可变长的轨迹. 关键的是,空间精度不需要重现一个自动递归模型精确的符号序列. VFlash因此在附加注释的原始语上进行训练,直接接受结构上有效的预测,而无需达成目标键协议. 在被评价的2D和3D机器人轨迹任务中,VFlash持续减少相对于自递解码的预测错误. 初步的单滚式测量表明,3D点运动预测的生成速度约为25x. 一个以VFlash计划为条件的世界行动模式在四个MolmoSpace任务套件中取得了70.2%的平均成功,而基线为62.6%。

blocks.en: Figure 1: VFlash is a generalist decoding framework for fast, accurate visual planning across Physical AI tasks such as robotics and autonomous driving. By aligning prediction blocks with the known structure of visual primitives, it enables parallel decoding of common structured outputs such as bounding boxes, variable-length 2D/3D trajectories, and dense point motion, while retaining verified speculative decoding for text and sub-task plans. Compared with autoregressive (AR) decoding, VFlash improves accuracy on 3D robot trajectory planning while substantially reducing decoding latency across NVIDIA platforms, including Jetson Thor, DGX Spark, and H100.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as high-level brains for physical AI systems, interpreting visual observations and task instructions to guide behavior in robotics and autonomous driving ( Gemini Robotics Team, 2025 ; Tian et al., 2025 ; NVIDIA et al., 2025 ) . Their reasoning need not be expressed solely in language. VLMs can formulate intermediate predictions as visual plans: points and bounding boxes identify relevant locations or
objects ( Yuan et al., 2025 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ) , while trajectories describe intended motion or forecast how a scene will evolve ( Gu et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2026a ) . Recent work uses spatial traces and visual primitives to guide action generation ( Li et al., 2025a ; Lee et al., 2025 ; Guo et al., 2026 ) .
These plans make spatial goals and anticipated motion explicit before action.
Each visual primitive has identifiable boundaries and an organized
coordinate layout.

blocks.en:
Generating such plans efficiently becomes increasingly important as their spatial detail grows.
Longer trajectories, additional objects, and joint 2D image and 3D
predictions require more coordinate tokens, which autoregressive VLMs
decode sequentially ( Chen et al., 2022 ; Bai et al., 2023 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ; Bai et al., 2025 ) .
For physical agents that update their plans as new observations arrive, sequential decoding limits spatial detail and update frequency under a fixed latency budget. This motivates decoding methods that can generate complete visual plans with fewer sequential forward passes while preserving their spatial accuracy.

blocks.en:
Parallel decoding offers a promising route to reducing this sequential cost, particularly for latency-sensitive physical AI systems operating at batch size one. Existing approaches include speculative decoding with parallel
verification ( Leviathan et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2025b ) and diffusion language models (dLLMs) with parallel denoising ( Nie et al., 2025 ; Arriola et al., 2025 ) . However, dLLMs often exhibit a speed–quality trade-off relative to autoregressive models ( Wu et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025 ) . DFlash combines these approaches using a lightweight block diffusion draft model to predict draft tokens in a single forward pass, followed by target verification that preserves the autoregressive model’s output
distribution ( Chen et al., 2026 ) . For visual outputs, LocateAnything exploits spatial structure through parallel box decoding ( Wang et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en: In this work, we introduce VFlash , a generalist decoding framework for physical AI (Figure 1 ) that accommodates both text (e.g., sub-task plans) and diverse visual primitives, such as bounding boxes, variable-length trajectories, and dense 3D motion predictions. Our study reveals an interesting observation: a lightweight diffusion drafter can even surpass its autoregressive target in spatial accuracy of the visual plans while decoding much faster. The structure of visual primitives helps explain this finding: once a primitive’s type, dimensionality, and length are specified, its boundaries and coordinate layout are known. Aligning draft blocks with these boundaries allows an entire geometric object to be predicted jointly, with tens to hundreds of tokens decoded in a single forward pass. These observations motivate aligning training and decoding with complete primitive boundaries and directly accepting structurally valid drafts without requiring token-level agreement with the target, while retaining verified decoding for text.
blocks.zh: 在本作中,我们引入了VFlash ,即物理AI(图1)的通论解码框架,既能容纳文本(如子任务计划),又能容纳多种视觉原始,如边框,可变长轨迹,以及密集的3D运动预测. 我们的研究揭示了一个有趣的观察:轻量级的传播起草器在视觉图的空间精确度方面甚至可以超过其自递性目标,同时解码速度要快得多。 视觉原始物的结构有助于解释这个发现:一旦一个原始物的种类,维度,长度被指定,它的边界和坐标布局就已知了. 将草稿块与这些边界对齐,使得整个几何对象可以被联合预测,在一次前传中解码了数十到数百个符号. 这些观察促使培训和解码与完全原始的边界一致,直接接受结构上有效的草稿而不需要与目标达成符号级的协议,同时保留经核实的文本解码.

blocks.en: At the center of VFlash is Flash Primitive Decoding (FPD), which uses the requested output structure to organize both drafter training and inference. A tool call specifies the size of a variable-length prediction, while the primitive type determines its coordinate layout. Conditioned on features from a frozen target VLM, a lightweight diffusion drafter learns to predict complete primitives from annotated spatial data. At inference, the decoder applies layout-specific constraints ( Willard and Louf, 2023 ; Geng et al., 2023 ) and accepts valid primitives in full. The target VLM supplies context for subsequent predictions, and ordinary text retains speculative decoding with target verification.
blocks.zh: VFlash的中心是Flash Primitive Drooding(FPD),它使用所要求的输出结构来组织起草器培训和推论. 一个工具调用指定了可变长预测的大小,而原始类型则决定其坐标布局. 以冻结目标VLM的特性为条件,一个轻量级扩散起草器学习从注释空间数据中预测完整的原始物. 推论,解码器应用了布局特有的限制(Willard and Louf, 2023;Geng等人, 2023),并完全接受有效的原始物. 目标VLM为后续预测提供上下文,普通文本保留了带有目标验证的投机解码.

blocks.en: We evaluate VFlash on 2D and 3D robot trajectories, bounding boxes, and dense 3D point motion forecasting, and study its use in downstream manipulation and driving. VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to its autoregressive target across the evaluated robot trajectory tasks. In the downstream robot manipulation pipeline shown in Figure 1 , it reduces inference latency by about 80% on both Jetson Thor and DGX Spark. These visual plans also provide useful conditioning for action models: on MolmoSpaces ( Kim et al., 2026b ) , a world action model ( Ye et al., 2026 ; NVIDIA, 2026c ) conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.
blocks.zh: 我们在2D和3D机器人轨迹,边框,密集的3D点运动预测上评价VFlash,并研究其在下游操纵和驾驶中的用途. VFlash在被评价的机器人轨迹任务中持续减少相对于其自动递归目标的预测错误. 在图1显示的下游机器人操纵管道中,它将Jetson Thor和DGX Spark的推论纬度都降低了约80%. 这些视觉计划还为行动模型提供了有用的条件:在MolmoSpaces(Kim等人,2026年b)上,一个以VFlash计划为条件的世界行动模型(Ye等人,2026年;NVIDIA,2026年c)上,四个任务套件的平均成功率为70.2%,而基线为62.6%.

blocks.en: Beyond acceleration, our work suggests a broader role for parallel decoding in multimodal systems. Lossless speculative decoding preserves the autoregressive target’s output distribution ( Leviathan et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2023a ) , whereas structured visual planning instead permits predictions to be judged by their spatial accuracy and usefulness for action, in the spirit of relaxed acceptance criteria ( Bachmann et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025c ) . VFlash enables a System-1 mode ( Kahneman, 2011 ) of visual planning in VLMs, producing fast, structured spatial predictions through joint coordinate decoding. This perspective interestingly connects to recent System-1 models such as Jev, which emphasize fast, typed decisions ( Almeida, 2026 ; Yu and Yao, 2026 ) . VFlash brings this perspective to complete geometric predictions, exploiting structure within each primitive. The resulting gains in both speed and spatial accuracy suggest that autoregressive decoding need not define the quality ceiling for visual outputs.
blocks.zh: 除了加速外,我们的工作还提议在多式联运系统中发挥更广泛的平行编码作用。 无损失的投机解码保留了自动递减目标的产出分布(Leviathan等人,2023年;Chen等人,2023年a年),而结构化的视觉规划则允许根据空间精确度和行动实用性来判断预测,并本着放宽接受标准的精神(Bachmann等人,2025年;Wang等人,2025年c年)。 VFlash在VLMs中实现了视觉规划的System-1模式(Kahneman,2011年),通过联合坐标解码生成快速,结构化的空间预测. 这一视角与Jev等近期的System-1模型有有趣的联系,Jev强调快速,打字的决定(Almeida,2026;Yu and Yao,2026). VFlash将这种视角带到完成几何预测,利用每个原始内部的结构. 由此在速度和空间准确性方面的增益表明,自递解码不需要确定视觉输出的质量上限。

blocks.en: 2.2 Flash primitive decoding
blocks.zh: 2.2 国家 闪光原始解码

blocks.en: Given visual observations and a task instruction, the VLM predicts spatial objects such as boxes, robot trajectories, or future point positions. Each prediction is a visual primitive with a schema s s specifying its type, coordinate dimensions, and extent. This fixes each coordinate’s role while leaving its value to be inferred from the input. A trajectory’s 2D image coordinates and 3D spatial coordinates can form one primitive and be predicted jointly. For variable-length predictions, a tool call declares the extent, which together with the primitive type determines the layout; for fixed-size predictions such as boxes, the type alone suffices. The structure is thus known before coordinate prediction, and each decoding block covers a complete primitive.

blocks.en: 2.3 Token representations
blocks.zh: 2.3 陈述

blocks.en:
Visual plans often require large, variable-length draft blocks.
For example, NAVSIM requires eight waypoints over four seconds,
while Waymo requires twenty over five seconds. Drafting such blocks
introduces challenges in format following and spatial accuracy.
We find that two design principles help address these challenges:
blocks.zh:
视觉图往往需要大块,可变长的区块草稿.
例如,NAVSIM 需要8个途径点 超过4秒,
而Waymo则需要20秒以上5秒 起草此类区块
在格式和空间准确性方面提出了挑战。
我们认为,两项设计原则有助于应对这些挑战:

blocks.en:
Boundary alignment decides what is predicted together:
each draft block covers one complete primitive, avoiding the splits
caused by fixed-length windows. The tool call declares the block
length, from which the waypoint count P P follows, and a shared layout
template accommodates different lengths, allowing the whole primitive
to be drafted in one pass.

mask token. This fixed-width grid preserves position roles and is
rendered back into the target’s text format, whose delimiters mark
block boundaries. Table 1 and Appendix A give the formats details.

blocks.en:
Base VLM. Most experiments use a customized embodied VLM combining
Qwen3-4B ( Yang et al., 2025 ) , a native-resolution MoonViT
encoder ( Kimi Team, 2025 ) , and an MLP connector. It is trained
progressively on general vision-language tasks,
grounding ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , embodied spatial
understanding, and joint 2D/3D trajectory prediction.
Coordinates for bounding box and trajectory use special tokens, with 2D image coordinates normalized
to 0–1,000 and 3D coordinates uniformly quantized within
predefined ranges. For dense motion prediction, we use the
released MolmoMotion-AR model ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) ,
retaining its text-based coordinate representation.

blocks.en: Figure 4 splits per-step latency into visual encoding, prefill, decoding, and the action model at batch size one on Jetson Thor, DGX Spark, and H100. Thor is an embedded platform for robots and vehicles and Spark a desktop-class system, typical on-device hardware for the System-1 visual planning of Section 1 ; H100 is the server reference. Appendix E gives the timing boundary and the full table. Across devices, VFlash cuts per-step latency 5.1–5.2 × \times on MolmoSpaces on Thor and Spark and 3.6 × \times on H100, and 3.4–3.6 × \times and 2.6 × \times on NAVSIM; on Waymo (Figure 5 ) the H100 reduction is 4.5 × \times . The gain comes almost entirely from decoding: under AR it takes 75–87% of each step on Thor, and VFlash cuts it 12–42 × \times while the other stages are unchanged.

blocks.en: AR decoding runs one 4B VLM pass per token (35–39 ms on Thor, 33–40 ms on Spark, 4.7–6.0 ms on H100), so decoding time grows roughly linearly with token count. Drafting predicts the remaining tokens of a 36–84-token primitive in one pass, taking 13–23 ms on Thor and 1–3 ms on H100. Verification still needs a target pass per block, so its benefit depends on the tokens committed per iteration. On MolmoSpaces, DFlash commits 5.5 tokens per iteration on subtask text but only 2.2 within trajectory blocks: a coordinate one bin off the target’s choice fails Eq. 2 even with small geometric error. DFlash thus only about halves decoding time. VFlash skips token-level verification for visual primitives, using one drafter pass and one target pass per primitive; the target pass updates the cache and extracts hidden states for the action head, amortized over the block. On Thor, decoding takes 72–78 ms as the driving primitive grows from 36 to 84 tokens, so denser plans add little latency over this range.

blocks.en: 4 Related Work
blocks.zh: 4 相关工作

blocks.en:
Embodied VLMs and visual plans. Embodied VLMs are increasingly used as high-level modules that turn
visual observations and language instructions into plans, affordances,
and trajectories ( Ji et al., 2025 ; BAAI RoboBrain Team, 2025 ; Gemini Robotics Team, 2025 ; Yuan et al., 2026b ; Dang et al., 2026 ) .
Spatial prediction is central to these models: points and boxes localize objects or
affordances ( Yuan et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2025a ; Deitke et al., 2025 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ) , while
traces describe intended or predicted motion ( Zhou et al., 2026a ; Wen et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2026a ) .
These visual plans can condition manipulation
policies ( Gu et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025a ; Liu et al., 2026b ; Tan et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) or be fed back as prompts ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) . Other work reasons
spatially before acting ( Lee et al., 2025 ; Fang et al., 2026 ; Guo et al., 2026 ) ,
predicts future states ( Kim et al., 2026a ; Ye et al., 2026 ) , or
plans driving trajectories from scene
understanding ( Tian et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025b ; NVIDIA et al., 2025 ) .
While this literature asks what embodied models should predict, we ask
how fast such spatial predictions can be produced. Token-by-token
coordinate generation makes every extra waypoint, object, or dimension
an additional decoding step.

Parallel and speculative decoding. Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by verifying multiple
drafted tokens in parallel ( Stern et al., 2018 ; Leviathan et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2023a ) .
Medusa, EAGLE, TIDAR, and DFlash explore different ways to produce these
drafts ( Cai et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2024a ; Liu et al., 2026c ; Chen et al., 2026 ) .
For visual outputs, LocateAnything decodes points and boxes as units,
but is limited to fixed-size 2D primitives ( Wang et al., 2026 ) .
Closest to this work, Spec-VLA accelerates OpenVLA by accepting draft action
tokens whose bins lie near the target’s ( Wang et al., 2025c ) . However, it still verifies each action token against the target and commits only 2.10 2.10 – 2.94 2.94 tokens per pass. Based on our finding that, for visual trajectory prediction, one-pass drafts are more accurate than the autoregressive target, VFlash
instead drafts the entire visual primitive in one pass rather than by agreement with the target.

blocks.en:
Embodied and System-1 models. In a deployed perception-action loop, VLM latency directly limits how
quickly the agent can react. Prior efficiency works mainly accelerate
the action execution pipeline, for example via action compression, parallel
action chunks, or flow matching ( Pertsch et al., 2025 ; Kim et al., 2025 ; Song et al., 2025 ; Black et al., 2024 ) .
Prior VLM-based planning, however, still often rely on highly autoregressive token decoding.
System-1 models such as Jev make fast typed decisions that downstream
applications can use directly ( Almeida, 2026 ) , and Visual Jev
answers many independent visual questions in parallel after one image
encoding ( Yu and Yao, 2026 ) . Our work can be seen as a relevant effort
that enables System-1 VLM spatial prediction. Within this context, our work
studies optimized token representation and decoding schemes systematically,
supporting both dedicated special tokens ( Chen et al., 2022 ) and plain
numbers ( Chen et al., 2023b ; Bai et al., 2023 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) .

blocks.en: In summary, VFlash uses DFlash-style drafting without target-token agreement, extending fast and accurate visual plan generation from LocateAnything’s parallel box decoding to richer and more general visual primitives that are useful for downstream embodied applications. It also enables more efficient decoding parallelism via systematic studies, in contrast to relevant or concurrent works.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented VFlash, which uses the known structure of visual primitives
to replace sequential coordinate generation with parallel prediction.
Our results show that useful spatial predictions need not reproduce an
autoregressive model’s output: direct drafts reduce robot trajectory
errors, while single-rollout timing estimates indicate approximately 25 × 25\times faster generation for 3D object point forecasting.
Plan-conditioned manipulation further demonstrates how these predictions
support downstream action generation. Future work will examine whether
generating multiple complementary primitives from shared observations
improves control within a fixed latency budget.

take over. A block whose length exceeds the remaining budget is
rejected before drafting.

blocks.en:

pass. Delimiter positions are fixed, coordinate positions are restricted
to number tokens, and coupled rules such as the pairing of out-of-frame
markers and the ordering of box corners are resolved by a small
selection loop over the logits already computed, with no further
network evaluation. The target then processes the completed block once
to update its cache, supply context features for the next block, and
predict the continuation. A schema-valid block is accepted in full
without token-level agreement. If validation fails, the target cache is
rolled back to the anchor and the block is regenerated by constrained
target AR from the first invalid position ( r = 0 r=0 for trajectories); the
drafter cache is reset afterwards. The DFlash baseline in
Section 3.3 instead applies 16-position blocks
and longest-prefix acceptance throughout the response, including inside
primitives.

blocks.en: The action head conditions on selected 2,560-dimensional final-layer states of the frozen target VLM. blocks.en: Ego motion inputs. The head uses 16 history entries, each containing position and heading ( x , y , ψ ) (x,y,\psi) , three availability indicators, and a relative timestamp. The resulting 112-dimensional vector is standardized using training-set statistics, with unavailable values zeroed and shorter histories left-padded. The 16-dimensional current-state vector contains four command indicators, four motion measurements, and eight availability indicators. Separate MLPs with 1,024 hidden units and LayerNorm map the history and current state to 384-dimensional embeddings.

blocks.en: Trajectory head. The ReCogDrive-derived head alternates eight self-attention and eight cross-attention blocks, with eight heads of width 48, adaptive normalization, and SwiGLU feed-forward layers. Each noisy waypoint is embedded with a learned index and a sinusoidal encoding of its physical future time; the index table supports up to 64 waypoints. Concatenating the waypoint embedding with the broadcast history embedding and masked mean VLM context yields 1,152 channels, which are projected to 384. The current-state and diffusion-timestep embeddings condition the transformer blocks. A 512-dimensional output projection followed by an MLP with 1,024 hidden units predicts three noise components per waypoint, for ( x , y , ψ ) (x,y,\psi) on NAVSIM and ( x , y ) (x,y) on Waymo, where the heading channel is masked. NAVSIM and Waymo use the same architecture with separately trained weights.

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning. After SFT, each head is fine-tuned with DiffGRPO ( Li et al., 2026 ) , which treats the five-step DDIM chain as a policy rollout. For every training scene, the head samples eight trajectories, scores them with a dataset-specific reward, and updates with group-standardized advantages. A behavior-cloning loss with weight 0.1 regularizes the update. It is the negative log-likelihood under the current head of denoising chains sampled from the frozen SFT head. No KL penalty is used. Both heads use an initial learning rate of 10 − 5 10^{-5} with cosine decay and no warmup. On NAVSIM the reward is PDMS from the non-reactive simulator ( Dauner et al., 2024 ) on the training split, with ego progress, time-to-collision within bound (TTC), and comfort weighted 10/5/2 during training against the official 5/5/2 used for evaluation. Training runs 10 epochs (6,650 updates) at batch size 16 per GPU on eight GPUs. The checkpoint is selected by PDMS on an internal validation split held out from navtrain by log (18,179 clips, Appendix F.5 ). On Waymo the reward is RFS from the official implementation on the 479 validation scenes. Training runs 20 epochs (300 updates) at batch size 4 per GPU on eight GPUs, and the checkpoint is selected on the same 479 scenes, so the selection score is in-sample. These settings are shared by all layout and context configurations. The VLM, its plans, and the conditioning states stay fixed, so the SFT and RL rows of Table 8 consume identical plans and differ only in head weights. Reported scores use the held-out test splits, which take no part in SFT, RL, or checkpoint selection.

blocks.en: Hardware and runtime. All measurements use batch size one and one request at a time on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (SM110), DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), and a single H100 80 GB (SM90). Our models run in a locally modified TensorRT-Edge-LLM ( NVIDIA, 2026b ) C++ runtime: vision encoder, target VLM, and drafter are exported through ONNX and compiled into TensorRT engines, TensorRT selects kernels for the exported operators, and Edge-LLM plugins supply attention (CuTe DSL FMHA for vision and prefill, XQA for decoding and speculative verification), cache updates, and positional encoding. Engines and kernel artifacts are built separately for each architecture. The stacks are CUDA 13.0 and TensorRT 10.15.2.7 on Thor, CUDA 13.0.88 and TensorRT 10.14.1.48 on Spark, and CUDA 12.9.86 and TensorRT 10.11.0.33 on H100. All Thor runs use a modified Edge-LLM 0.9.0 tree; all Spark runs and the H100 MolmoSpaces runs use Edge-LLM 0.10.1; the H100 driving runs use the 0.9.0 tree with an SM90 attention bridge. Vision, target, and draft engines run in FP16 with FP16 KV caches; no weight or KV quantization is used.
blocks.zh: 硬件和运行时间。 所有测量都使用一次批量大小和一次请求NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor(SM110),DGX Spark(GB10,SM121),以及单H100 80 GB(SM90). 我们的模型运行在本地修改的TensorRT-Edge-LLM(NVIDIA, 2026b) C++运行时间:视觉编码器,目标VLM,以及起草器通过ONNX输出并编成TensorRT引擎,TensorRT为输出的操作员选择内核,Edge-LLM插件提供注意(CuTe DSL FMA用于视觉和预填充,QQA用于解码和投机性验证),缓存更新和位置编码. 发动机和内核文物为每个建筑分别建造. 这些堆栈是索尔岛的CUDA 13.0和TensorRT 10.15.2.7,火花岛的CUDA 13.0.88和TensorRT 10.14.48,H100岛的CUDA 12.9.86和TensorRT 10.11.0.33。 全体 Thor运行使用经过修改的Edge-LLM 0.9.0树;所有Spark运行和H100 MollmoSpace运行使用Edge-LLM 0.10.1;H100驱动运行使用具有SM90关注桥的0.9.0树. 远景,目标,和草稿引擎在FP16中运行,有FP16 KV缓存;没有使用重量或KV量化.

blocks.en: Decoders. AR performs target-only single-token decoding. DFlash drafts 16-token blocks and accepts the longest prefix that matches the target’s greedy choice exactly, plus the correction token; numeric coordinates receive no tolerance. VFlash decodes text with the same verified blocks, then drafts the whole primitive in one unverified block (54 tokens for MolmoSpaces, 36 for NAVSIM, 84 for Waymo) and runs one cached target prefill over the accepted block, the EOS token, and end-of-text padding to produce the hidden states the action model consumes. This prefill is counted as decoding. For MolmoSpaces the prefill retains 512 non-image positions from all 36 target layers; for driving it exports the final layer only, padded to 2,200 positions on NAVSIM. In both pipelines the fixed tool-call JSON is supplied rather than generated; on MolmoSpaces it is committed inside the text verification pass, and on driving the think-and-tool prefix precedes generation, so decoding covers exactly the primitive. All decoders use the same supplied tool-call JSON and the same primitive length. AR and DFlash reuse the target states computed during generation and need no separate feature pass.
blocks.zh: 解码器. AR只执行目标单键解码. DFlash 草稿为 16- token 块, 并接受与目标贪婪选择完全吻合的最长前缀, 加上校正符号; 数字坐标不会得到容忍度 。 VFlash将文本解码为同一经验证的块,然后在一个未经验证的块中起草整个原始的块(MolmoSpaces的54个令牌,NAVSIM的36个令牌,Waymo的84个令牌),并在接受的块上运行一个缓存的目标预填,EOS令牌,以及文字末端的补丁来生成动作模型所消耗的隐藏状态. 此预填被算作解码 。 为莫尔莫 预填空格保留所有36个目标层的512个非图像位置;由于驱动它只输出最后一层,在NAVSIM上添加到2200个位置. 在两个管道中,固定工具呼叫JSON是提供而不是生成的;在MolmoSpaces上,它被承诺在文本验证证内,在驱动思维和工具前缀在生成前,所以解码完全覆盖了原始的. 所有解码器都使用同样的提供的工具调用JSON和相同的原始长度. AR和DFlash在生成过程中重新使用目标状态,不需要单独的特性通行证。

blocks.en: Action models. The MolmoSpaces WAM runs one WAN encoder call and four DiT calls (joint, action, joint, action) inside a CUDA graph, with BF16 DiT weights and FP16 attention through a custom head-dimension-128 CuTe DSL kernel on Thor and Spark; the H100 baseline uses native TensorRT attention. The ReCogDrive head is a BF16 TensorRT engine containing feature encoding and the DDIM sampler. Latency profiles unroll ten DDIM steps to match the ten-step Qwen-Drive planner; the quality results of Table 8 use five steps (Appendix F.5 ).
blocks.zh: 行动模式。 MolmoSpaces WAM在CUDA图中运行一个WAN编码器呼叫器和四个DiT呼叫器(联合,动作,联合,动作),通过Thor和Spark上的定制头-dimension-128 CuTe DSL内核,具有BF16 DiT重量和FP16关注度;H100基线使用本地的TensorRT关注度. ReCogDrive头是一个BF16 TensorRT引擎,包含特征编码和DDIM采样器.  Latency 剖面图 解卷十 DDIM 步骤,以匹配十步 Quen-Drive 规划器; 表 8 的质量结果使用五个步骤( Appendix F.5 ).

blocks.en: Qwen-Drive-1.0. We run the released checkpoint in its reasoning planning mode with greedy decoding. On Thor and Spark it uses a customized Edge-LLM 0.9.0 runtime with CuTe DSL Gated DeltaNet kernels for its 24 linear-attention layers and FMHA/XQA for its eight full-attention layers; on H100 it uses the TensorRT-LLM backend with FlashInfer kernels. Its 1.04B flow-matching planner is a separate TensorRT engine with BF16 weights, FP16 attention, and ten Euler steps in a CUDA graph. Inputs are one 1600 × \times 896 front image on NAVSIM (1,400 visual tokens; 1600 × \times 800 in the Thor runs) and three 800 × \times 896 images on Waymo (2,100 tokens). The Fast-dDrive value in Figure 5 is taken from its paper and was not measured here.

blocks.en: Timing protocol. Each request starts from fresh vision computation and model state. CUDA events bracket each stage (preprocessing and vision encoding, prefill, decoding, action model) and are summed over all calls within a request; these intervals include host launch gaps and are not kernel-only durations. Model loading, engine construction, graph capture, warmup, image loading and CPU preprocessing outside the instrumented modules, and output detokenization are excluded. Repeat counts differ by run: the Thor MolmoSpaces pipeline uses 24 records and ten passes after five warmups; the Spark and H100 robotics runs one pass over the same 24 records after five warmups; driving runs five records and ten passes after five warmups; the Qwen-Drive H100 run five scenes twice after five warmups. Reported per-step latency is the sum of stage means. Within each device and task, the vision, prefill, and action-model means are shared across decoders; decoding is profiled separately. The MolmoSpaces AR decoding time comes from an earlier standalone profile with an output-only target engine, whereas the VFlash decoding time includes the all-layer feature completion described above; the driving decoders share one target-engine configuration.
blocks.zh: 时间协议。 每个请求都从新视觉计算和模型状态开始. CUDA事件将每个阶段(预处理和视觉编码、预填充、解码、行动模型)置于括号内,并在请求中的所有呼叫中进行汇总;这些间隔包括主机发射缺口,并非仅限内核持续时间。 模型加载,引擎构造,图捕捉,热身,图像加载和CPU预处理在仪表模块之外,输出解调功能被排除在外. 重复计数因运行而异:托尔莫摩斯太空管使用24个记录和5个热身后10个通过;火花和H100机器人在5个热身后运行1个通过同样的24个记录;驾驶运行5个记录和5个热身后运行10个通过;Quen-Drive H100在5个热身后运行5个场景两次. 报告的每步延迟是舞台手段的总和. 在每个设备和任务中,视觉,预填,和行动模型手段在解码器之间共享;解码被单独剖析. MolmoSpaces AR解码时间来自较早的具有只输出目标引擎的独立配置,而VFlash解码时间包括上述全层特性完成;驱动解码器共享一个目标引擎配置.

F.5 Autonomous Driving
blocks.zh: F.5 自主驾驶

blocks.en: Splits and data separation. NAVSIM training uses navtrain, divided by log into 85,109 training and 18,179 internal validation clips; SFT and RL fit on the former, and checkpoints are selected on the latter by PDMS. Test scores use all 12,146 navtest scenes. Waymo SFT uses the official training split. The 479 validation scenes provide the RL reward and are used to select both SFT and RL checkpoints by RFS. Test scores come from the official test split. Neither test split enters SFT, RL, or checkpoint selection. The upstream VLM was fine-tuned on all of navtrain and on the Waymo training split. The NAVSIM internal validation clips are therefore held out from action-head fitting but not from VLM fine-tuning. The Waymo validation scenes and both test splits are excluded from VLM fine-tuning.
blocks.zh: 分割与数据分离. NAVSIM训练使用导航列车,按日志分为85,109次训练和18,179次内部验证短片;SFT和RL适合前者,而PDMS则选择后者上的检查站. 测试分数使用所有12,146个导航场景. Waymo SFT采用正式训练分法. 479个验证场景提供了RL奖励,并被RFS用于选择SFT和RL两个检查站. 测试分数来自正式测试分数. 测试拆分既不进入SFT,RL,也不进入检查站选择. 上游的VLM对所有航海和Waymo训练进行了微调。 因此,NAVSIM内部验证片段是从行动头装配而来,而不是从VLM微调而来。 Waymo验证场景和两个测试分裂都被排除在VLM微调之外.

blocks.en: Scoring. Each scene is evaluated once: the initial Gaussian noise is seeded from the clip identifier, and five deterministic DDIM steps produce the trajectory. On NAVSIM the head’s eight ( x , y , ψ ) (x,y,\psi) waypoints at 2 Hz are scored by the official non-reactive PDM simulator ( Dauner et al., 2024 ) with the standard 5/5/2 weights for ego progress, time-to-collision within bound, and comfort. On Waymo the head’s twenty ( x , y ) (x,y) waypoints at 4 Hz are scored by the official RFS implementation, and ADE at 3 s and 5 s averages Euclidean position error over the horizon; both require a complete prediction through the horizon.
blocks.zh: S. 每个场景都要经过一次评价:最初的高斯噪声从剪辑标识符中播种,五个定型DDIM步骤产生轨迹. 在NAVSIM上,头部的8(x,y,ψ)(x,y,\psi)方向点数为2赫兹,由官方的非反应性PDM模拟器(Dauner等人,2024年)得分,标准为5/5/2重量,以达到自我进步、约束内的时间和舒适度。 在Waymo上,头部20(x,y)(x,y)位点在4Hz被正式的 RFS 执行得分,而ADE 位点平均为3s和5s的Euclidean 位点误差;两者都需要通过地平线进行完整的预测.

blocks.en: Compared methods. DiffusionLTF is the DiffusionDrive-based policy released with Open X-AV ( Nguyen et al., 2025 ) ; its scores are taken from the WOD-E2E leaderboard. Qwen-Drive-1.0 ( Zhou et al., 2026b ) couples Qwen3.5-4B with a flow-matching planner conditioned on VLM representations of the scene and an autoregressively generated text reasoning trace; its RL stage, like ours, optimizes only the planner with PDMS and RFS rewards. Fast-dDrive ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) is a block-diffusion dLLM that generates reasoning and trajectory as structured text and reports Waymo results only. Both reason in text where VFlash uses a visual plan. Latency measurement conditions for these methods, including our own measurement of Qwen-Drive-1.0, are given in Appendix E .
